title: The gates of hell (Matthew 16:13–28)
hook: who do people say you are, and who do you say? Peter answers for himself
tomorrow: what do you do when you're too scared to even look up?

segments.voice: A week from the storeroom to the boat: new and old, compassion in grief, a hand reaching out, what comes from the heart, a mother who kept asking, and yesterday, a little leaven that won't stay little.
screen: `A LITTLE LEAVEN.` → `A WEEK FROM STOREROOM TO BOAT.`

segments.voice: A bio line. A yearbook quote. A college essay that asks, in three words, who are you? It's easy to fill the space with what other people say. Near Caesarea Philippi, Jesus asks his friends that first question: "Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?" The answers come easily, the way talk does: John the Baptist, Elias, Jeremias, one of the prophets. Then he turns it around, and there's nowhere to hide behind anyone else's opinion: "But whom say ye that I am?"
screen: `WHO ARE YOU?` → `WHOM DO MEN SAY?` → `BUT WHOM SAY YE?`

segments.voice: Peter answers: "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God." Jesus calls him blessed, and says: "thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it." In Matthew's Greek, Peter is Petros and rock is petra, a play on words built in. Where the King James says hell, the Greek says Hades, the realm of the dead. Even death's gates won't hold out. Churches read the rock differently. In Catholic teaching, it's Peter himself, with the keys passing to his successors, the bishops of Rome. Some Orthodox and Protestant readers hear the rock as Peter's confession of faith; some hear Christ himself. The confession, thou art the Christ, is the shared ground. And Matthew keeps Peter human. A few verses later, Peter rebukes Jesus for speaking of his coming suffering, and hears: "Get thee behind me, Satan." The rock and the stumbling block, in one chapter.
screen: `THOU ART THE CHRIST.` · `PETROS AND PETRA.` · `HADES' GATES WON'T HOLD.` · `ONE CONFESSION, READ THREE WAYS.`

segments.voice: If you pray, you can say Peter's words aloud, slowly: thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God. If not, say one plain sentence out loud about something you hold to be true, in your own words, not anyone else's. Then let the room be quiet while you breathe.
The gates of hell. In the King James, Hades in the Greek: the gates of death, which Jesus says won't prevail against what he builds.
For the week's end: the gates shall not prevail, not even the gates of death. Week done.
